sentences.text: Mr. Santanu Saha vs Unknown on 8 April, 2025

Author: Jay Sengupta
Bench: Jay Sengupta
Court No. C.R.R. 1590 of 2025 Item 91 ssi 08.04.
In the matter of:- Mr. Santanu Saha Mr. Abhimanyu Banerjee Mr. Arnab Saha Ms. Priyanka Yadav
...for the petitioner Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits as follows.

A charge sheet has been submitted against the petitioner, the husband and the other in laws of the defacto complainant under Sections 498A, 406 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code read with Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The petitioner is working in Merchant Navy.
A careful reading of the FIR would reveal that there is hardly any allegation made against the husband.
The main allegations are against the other in laws because the husband was most of the times away on his work.
Any further continuation of the proceeding against the husband would be an abuse in the process of Court.
There is also a huge delay in lodging the FIR.
There are even correspondences that would show that there were talks of settlement of dispute before the FIR was lodged.
The next date for hearing is on 02.05.205.
Let the petitioner serve a copy of this application through the learned Public Prosecutor and upon the opposite party no.2 by speed post with acknowledgment due, within a week.
An affidavit of service to that effect shall be filed on the next date.
List this matter for hearing under the heading "Motion" after two weeks.
The impugned proceeding shall remain stayed for a period of three weeks from this date.
Parties shall be at liberty to pray for extension or modification or vacating of the interim order upon notice to the other side.
The State shall produce the case diary on the next date.
Urgent photostat certified copy of this order be supplied to the parties, if applied for, as early as possible.

(Jay Sengupta, J.)
